title: Bubbling Moon round 2: the pipe slide at Pip's size, flow frames, a tall support leg, the giant bubble
prompt:
THE WORLD: the Bubbling Moon, a strange, silly and slightly sad moon in a children's game (never scary). Its milk lakes have dried into cracked, glossy white crust that mirrors the sky. Giant cheese craters full of Swiss-cheese holes are the pits. Bubbles of old milk pop up out of the ground on a slow beat, as if the moon had hiccups. A big wobbling curd drifts across the dry lake like a slow boat. The cats built an old, half-finished, high-tech milk pumping station here: steel grey with orange and yellow trim, rust, paw-print logos and coloured cables. Palette: milk white, cream, butter yellow, cheese orange, pale lavender and blue-grey shadows, a deep violet night sky.

You are drawing a SPRITE SHEET for the Bubbling Moon level of a side-view platformer. Everything is seen strictly from the side (a 2D platformer; not isometric, not top-down).

FORMAT
- One PNG, 3840 x 2160, landscape. Background: ONE flat, solid, bright pure green (#00FF00) everywhere behind the items. No checkerboard, no scenery, no ground strip, no frames or boxes round items, no title, no legend. No bright green inside the items (the green eyes of Miss Clou and any mould are a darker, duller green).
- Follow the row plan below, rows from top to bottom, items from left to right, exactly the items listed (one drawing each, nothing extra, nothing missing; the frames of one animation are the same size, side by side, on the same ground line, identical in colours and proportions). Items stand on a common ground line in their row. Leave at least 6 art pixels (24 image pixels) of empty green all round every item; no item may touch another item or the edge.
- Under each item a short label in small plain white text (catalogue style) with a clear gap between the label and the item above it and the tops of the items in the row below. The label is the item's name exactly as given in quotes. Keep the labels short.

STYLE (a program cuts this picture into pixel-art sprites for a game, so follow it exactly)
- TRUE 16-bit (Super Nintendo style) pixel art on a strict fixed grid: every art pixel is a perfectly square, evenly coloured 4 x 4 block of image pixels, so every pixel can be counted by eye. Edges of shapes are clean staircases of whole square pixels: never smooth curves, never soft or noisy shading, never JPEG-like speckle, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no blur, no glow halos, no dithering noise, no drop shadows, no cast shadows on the ground. Each shade is ONE exact flat colour; use only a small palette of about 32 colours for the whole picture, the same colour every time it is used.
- A clean, continuous, dark near-black-brown (#1A1410) outline exactly 1 art pixel (4 image pixels) thick round EVERY item (except where a line says "no outline", for soft things), also round white, cream and pale items so they stand out from the green; used ONLY for outlines. No fill colour darker than #40382F. Inside the outline shade each material with 2 or 3 flat tones and a few hard-edged pixel highlights, like the references.
- Match the three attached reference pictures in pixel size, line weight, saturation and level of detail: (1) the game's own props sheet (its green ground is the ground to use here too); (2) a finished sheet of this level's pumping-station props: match its pixel size, line weight, colours and shading exactly; (3) the hero, Pip the mouse astronaut: he is 49 art pixels tall, which fixes the scale of everything.
- SCALE: Pip is 49 art pixels (196 image pixels) tall; everything is drawn at that same pixel size. Sizes below are in art pixels (width x height), only roughly.
- Glass, bubbles and windows are drawn in opaque pale colours with a white highlight: nothing is see-through, and nothing is drawn behind an item.
- No text inside the items except where a line gives the words. Seen strictly from the side (a 2D platformer), light from the upper left.

ROW PLAN (5 rows)
Row 1, THE SLIDE PIPES (a big transparent glass tube filled with milk: Pip, a mouse 49 art pixels tall, must fit INSIDE it, so the clear inside is at least 80 art pixels tall (more than one and a half Pip heights: the whole tube is about 100 art pixels tall) and flat, unobstructed, drawn in opaque cream-white milk with a few pale streaks and white glass highlights; the glass shell is pale blue-white with a thin dark outline; a steel collar with an orange band every 70 art pixels; seen from the side) (every item in this row belongs to the group "pipeslide"), 5 items: 1 "straight" a straight piece that tiles end to end (140 x 100); 2 "end-left" the open mouth on the LEFT end: a steel flange ring, the tube opening towards the left (100 x 100); 3 "end-right" the open end on the RIGHT end that spits things out: a flange ring and a small spout of milk drips (110 x 100); 4 "tee-up" a T junction: a horizontal tube with a branch going UP (140 x 170); 5 "tee-down" a T junction: a horizontal tube with a branch going DOWN (140 x 170).
Row 2, MORE SLIDE PIPES (same look) (every item in this row belongs to the group "pipeslide"), 3 items: 1 "shaft" a vertical straight shaft that tiles top to bottom (100 x 140); 2 "corner-up" a corner: the tube comes in from the left and turns UP (120 x 120); 3 "corner-down" a corner: the tube comes in from the left and turns DOWN (120 x 120).
Row 3, THE FLOW (only the milk inside a straight piece, 140 x 80 each, four frames of one loop; the streaks of the thick milk slide to the right a little in every frame and the last frame continues into the first, so it tiles) (every item in this row belongs to the group "pipeslide"), 4 items: 1 "flow-1" cream-white milk with pale blue-white streaks, frame 1; 2 "flow-2" frame 2: the streaks moved right; 3 "flow-3" frame 3; 4 "flow-4" frame 4.
Row 4, THE PIPELINE LEG (every item in this row belongs to the group "station"), 1 item: 1 "main-support-tall" a tall A-frame steel support leg for a giant pipeline, with cross bracing, rivets and an orange band, standing on a base plate (44 x 112).
Row 5, THE GIANT BUBBLE (every item in this row belongs to the group "milk"), 1 item: 1 "bubble-giant" one giant milk bubble, milky white with a cream rim and bright white highlights, pale blue shadow, drawn with fine pixels so it does not look chunky (150 x 150).
